text: Does my content promote misogynistic ideas? Another interesting question. Hello Ilyas, I watch a lot of your content. I agree that data always matters, but I was wondering about your audience. Because you push content geared towards men, I realize I see a lot of men who seemingly aren't exactly watching your content for the substance, rather the owning of a typically feminist idea. Most of your comments are flooded with strangely misogynistic ideas or phrases, especially when it comes to advice on specific situations with a woman. I hope it's not your intention, but I'd like to know your thoughts, perhaps where you stand in general. Thanks! Honestly, I appreciate this question. I'm not sure about most of the comments feeding that pattern, but some definitely do. That part is fair. Is it my intention? No, and I think most of my regular viewers understand that. What I actually do is talk about men's issues and push back against misandry, not push for misogyny. To me, both misandry and misogyny are radical and both are dangerous. I genuinely believe men and women aren't enemies, we need each other, and I say that often. Both sides have real problems worth talking about, I just tend to focus more on the men's side, because that's the side I understand better. And I regularly remind people in my videos, there are bad men and bad women out there, sure, but there are also plenty of good ones on both sides. Now, as for whether I'm going to do something about certain comments, here's how I see it. I focus on what I can control, which is my content and the message I'm sending. How people receive it, how they react, what they choose to say in the comments, that's not really in my hands. I'm also a strong believer in free expression. If people want to share opinions I personally disagree with, go ahead, I actually encourage it, because I know I have viewers across the spectrum and now they get to compete on who can make the better argument. And let's be real, even if I constantly said, guys, don't say this, this is bad, the people writing those comments aren't going to suddenly think, oh, Ilya said it, now I see it is bad. If my videos, which I put real effort into, aren't changing their minds, expecting a disclaimer to do is just naive. Same logic applies, by the way, to guys like Professor Neil, Simple Black Theory, that guy Nick, or Brenna Paris. You think after my breakdowns they go, damn, what are we doing, we are misrepresenting the data, we are being dishonest here. Yeah, sure, I'm hopeful, but I'm not naive. And honestly, the issue isn't that they can't see it, I bet some of them know exactly what they're doing. The real problem is they are prisoners of their own audience. The second they say something against the main narrative their viewers expect, they lose them, so they are stuck. My channel is built differently, at least I hope so. I try to promote curiosity and critical thinking. I know that sooner or later I say something some of my viewers wouldn't agree with, and that's already happened with videos like Is Being Gay Normal? or Can Men and Women Be Friends? That's fine, you are allowed to disagree with me, you are encouraged to write your opinions in the comments. But if you do, I just ask that you be able to explain why this is your opinion, and that you are willing to actually listen to another perspective.
